choices: Only material seeds 9000–9015 are analyzed; other seeds, if present, are treated as outside the preregistered main run.
Items are keyed by id, as specified for deduplication and bootstrap ordering. A given id must have consistent seed and truth across its records.

For each arm, the failure-rate denominator is the number of distinct item ids observed for that arm before complete-item exclusion. Missing cells for these ids count as failures. Entirely unobserved items cannot be recovered from this file; no unobserved ids or material exclusions are invented.
Last record means last occurrence in JSONL file order for each (model, id, cell), including when that last record is a failure.
The prompt-presence check applies literally to every in-scope input row, including superseded rows; cell names determine the expected prompt flags.

Apart from failure rates and the every-row prompt check, manipulation-check rates use the same jointly complete items as the contrasts. An empty denominator, including an absent truth group, fails the applicable check.

A failed manipulation check in either arm makes both assignments descriptive, because each assignment involves both arms. Fewer than 144 complete items also makes both assignments descriptive. Such primary results retain their estimates and intervals but have q=null, label=deskriptiv, confirmed=false.
Decision rules are applied in their listed order: supporting evidence first, then practically null, then prediction excluded, then undecided.
Descriptive bootstrap seeds 445–449 are assigned in output order to K0Z, K0V, R1V, R2V, B4Z. Each assignment and each quantity starts a fresh random.Random with its specified seed.

n_complete_seeds counts distinct material seeds represented by at least one jointly complete item. It is not the complete-item count used for the 144-item gate, and does not impose a seed-level exclusion rule.

The fixed output schema reports the nine requested item-level quantities per assignment. Additional preregistered descriptive cell/domain rates and the 5%-broken prevalence illustration are computed internally but have no dedicated output fields.

The prevalence illustration assumes the confirmation rate on actually broken items transports to a population with 5% broken items; expected overlooked errors per 1000 are 1000*0.05 times that rate, separately for each N,T cell.
The two attested harness checks are accepted as passed and are not recomputed.
